title: Ines and the Salt
premise: Edmund Halloran, a beast-speaker who must hide his gift in a guild that trades in impossible things, inherits a dying stranger's map to a door out of Vell — a country erased from every record and memory except his own. Pursued by the guild's Salt Wardens and shadowed by the stranger's vengeful daughter, Edmund discovers the map can only be read aloud by someone the vanished land still remembers. To open the door he must choose between exposing his forbidden gift and abandoning the ragtag found family that has become his only home; in the end he speaks the truth of what he is, opens the way for those he loves, and stays behind as the last living memory of Vell.
about_author: Astrid Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer appear on any chart. She writes quiet, aching fantasy about people who keep secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In the guildhouse of Corvane & Sons, Edmund balances accounts of bottled storms and caged echoes while concealing the fact that he can hear the beasts in the cellar talking. A dying stranger collapses at the counting desk, pressing a salt-stained map into his hands and whispering a name Edmund has never heard but somehow knows. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Interrogating the cellar rats, Edmund learns they remember a country called Vell that no human does — and that the dying man was its last cartographer. The Salt Wardens arrive to collect 'guild property,' forcing Edmund to lie badly and flee with the map hidden in a ledger. He gathers unlikely allies: pickpocket Sefa and the disgraced warden Brannoc. Emotional beat: first taste of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: A Daughter Made of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The stranger's daughter, Ilse, catches up with them, furious that her father gave away the inheritance she was owed. She joins them only to take the map back, testing Edmund's trust at every turn. The group deciphers the map's first clue: it must be read where salt water meets fresh. Emotional beat: friction between grief and greed.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc. In a border market where identities are traded like spices, Brannoc bargains with an old informant and learns the Wardens have posted a price on all their heads — and that Edmund's gift is already suspected. He covers for Edmund without being asked, the first act of unearned loyalty he has offered anyone. Emotional beat: guilt softening into devotion.

chapters.title: Where the Rivers Argue
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the confluence, Edmund reads the map aloud and hears it answer him in his mother's voice — proof Vell remembers him, though he cannot remember Vell. The reading tears a seam in the air showing a white doorway, then seals itself: three more readings are needed, each costing the reader a memory. Emotional beat: wonder tangled with fear of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Ilse's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse secretly offers herself as reader for the second gate, hoping to reach her father's homeland before it finishes forgetting her. The reading costs her the memory of her father's face, and she emerges changed — gentler, and suddenly allied with Edmund rather than against him. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into kinship.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wounds
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The Wardens ambush the group; Brannoc is captured and interrogated with salt that burns lies out of flesh. Edmund must decide whether to surrender himself or use his beast-speaker gift openly to turn the wardens' hounds. He chooses exposure, commanding the hounds to turn, and the company escapes but Edmund is now marked as forbidden. Emotional beat: loyalty outweighing safety.

chapters.title: The Third Reading
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa volunteers for the third gate to prove she belongs to this makeshift family, losing her memory of the streets that raised her. But the reading reveals the terrible truth: the final gate requires a reader whom Vell fully remembers — and that is Edmund alone, whose memories will be consumed entirely. Emotional beat: found family confronting sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vell
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Hunted to the threshold, Edmund performs the final reading while Ilse and Sefa hold off the Wardens and Brannoc returns, freed, to stand beside him. The door opens onto the ordinary world; one by one his family steps through into lives that will finally be safe. Edmund feels his own memories thinning like smoke. Emotional beat: love at the edge of oblivion.

chapters.title: Ines and the Salt
chapters.summary: POV Edmund (epilogue). Edmund remains as Vell's last remembered soul, keeper of a country only beasts and salt can name — yet the ledger he left behind reaches his friends years later, written in a hand that remembers them still. Ilse plants her father's map on a grave of white sand; Sefa teaches children the names of vanished rivers. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with enduring connection.
